subject: ventures/wedding-day-timeline-builder
professional: a full-service wedding planner / lead wedding photographer who writes day-of timelines for clients (checks first: portrait block lengths, hair and makeup back-timing, guests seated before ceremony, sunset time and where golden-hour portraits land, dinner length and that the vendor sheets agree)

evidence.correctness: Ran node on calc.mjs. Sunset recomputed against sources the author did not write: NYC 2026-06-20 tool 8:30 PM EDT vs known almanac ~8:31 PM; Seattle 2026-12-21 tool 4:20 PM PST vs known ~4:20 PM; Sydney 2026-12-21 tool 8:05 PM AEDT vs known ~8:05 PM (almanac values from memory, no live USNO fetch). Timeline arithmetic by hand from the sample (Charleston, 4:30 PM ceremony, 8 party, 10 groups, first look): family 10x3+5=35, party 10+16=26, couple 30, first look 15; back-timed from 4:10 hides block gives first look 2:24 PM, matches output; hair makespan for 5 people on 2 artists greedy LPT (90,60,60,60,60): artist1 90+60=150, artist2 60+60+60=180, hand-checked 180 min, start 10:44 AM, matches. Without first look: 96 min of portraits after 5:00 PM ceremony ends = 6:36 PM, +10 = 6:46 vs 6:00 planned, stretch 46 min, matches the guide page. Dinner 40+0.2x120=64 -> 65 min plausible (plated 60-75 min). No wrong number found. Limit: sunset almanac values recalled, not fetched.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README feature in code and the sample run: hair/makeup split across artists (works), first look and no-first-look plans with stretch warning (works), ceremony/travel/cocktail/entrance/dances/dinner/toasts/cake/dancing back-timed from curfew (works), NOAA sunset plus 15-min golden overlay (works), ceremony advisor 10:00-19:30 every half hour (adviseCeremonyTimes), six vendor views plus ICS/CSV/text, save/load state (functions exist, tested). Did not load the page in a browser; page wiring not exercised beyond page.test.mjs. No TODO stubs found. VENTURE.yaml stage is prototype, hypotheses untested.
evidence.verification: node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs: 36 pass, 0 fail. Seeded three mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted by git checkout (git status clean): (1) family portrait setup +5 -> +0: all 23 calc tests still pass (SURVIVED); (2) coupleMin 30 -> 25: all pass (SURVIVED); (3) hair scheduler picks busiest artist instead of freest: test 7 failed (caught). Core duration constants and the portrait-block arithmetic are not pinned except through the guide page recomputation, which evidently does not catch them either; the scheduler and sunset are well tested.
evidence.craft: Read all of calc.mjs (458 lines), checked usage.mjs and tests. Pure functions, clear input normalisation with clamping, named constants, sensible structure. Defects: icsEscape uses "\;" inside a JS string which is just ";" so semicolons in titles/notes are not escaped (RFC 5545 requires \;), confirmed by running timelineIcs; ICS uses floating local times with a constant DTSTAMP default; the 'Officiant arrives' and 'Guests arrive' events are hard-coded offsets; a Dinner event is found by title prefix in scoreDay (string coupling); CITIES hard-codes a UTC offset lookup via Intl which is fine. sitemap.xml, robots.txt and canonical use relative URLs, which are invalid for crawlers.
evidence.claims: Backed: no-upload privacy (no network calls found in calc/usage), 15/30/10+2n/3-per-group conventions and the 106-minute total (guide line 32, arithmetic checked), 6:36 PM and 46 extra minutes (recomputed), first-look 2:24 PM and golden at 5:41 PM (matches run), disclaimer and no-warranty text present, opt-out for usage counters present. Not backed or inconsistent: FAQ and page say sunset portraits start 'about 30 minutes before sunset', but the worked example (and sample day) place them at 5:41 PM, 65 minutes before the 6:46 PM sunset (the ideal slot is blocked by the entrance, dances and dinner), so the headline claim overstates; the golden hour is then well before the actual golden hour for that date. llms.txt links to duncan-haywood.github.io, a retired host (live site is marisstella.app). Test suite 'confirms ... couple is never double-booked' is not true by construction since the golden overlay is flagged couple:false and warnings do not cover overlap.
evidence.fitness: Walked a planner's job: entered the sample (Charleston, October, 120 guests, first look), got a coherent minute-by-minute day from 10:44 AM hair to 10:30 PM send-off, vendor sheets, ICS and CSV, with warnings when the program overruns or dancing is short. A photographer or couple could use it as a first draft. Gaps a planner would hit: only 33 preset cities (others need manual lat/lon and a UTC offset); no editing of individual events or drag adjustment; no multiple cultural/religious ceremony blocks, receiving line, or separate photo-booth/ grand exit slots; golden-hour slot ignores whether the couple wants to leave a reception. Not loaded in a browser.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard photography and planning practice: first look 15 min, couple portraits 30, wedding party 20-30 min, family 30-45 min, guests seated 15-30 min before, hair and makeup 60-90 min per client, plated dinner 60-75 min, 4 min toasts, 10 min cake. Durations are all in range and labelled as conventions. Departures: sunset portraits conventionally 15-30 minutes before sunset, not the 65 minutes the tool produced in its own flagship example; no buffer for travel to portrait locations on a same-venue first look; family list at 3 min/group is optimistic for large formal groups; no receiving line. Sunset method (NOAA) is the professional standard for planning.

defects.what: Worked example and sample place sunset portraits 65 minutes before sunset while the FAQ and page text promise about 30 minutes before; the slot search silently accepts a 35-minute miss and the page does not say so
Tests do not pin the portrait-block constants: changing family setup +5 to +0 or couple portraits 30 to 25 leaves all 23 engine tests green
icsEscape does not escape semicolons (a backslash-semicolon in a JS string literal is just a semicolon), so titles or notes containing semicolons produce invalid ICS text per RFC 5545
sitemap.xml, robots.txt Sitemap line and canonical link use relative URLs, invalid for crawlers
llms.txt points to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host instead of marisstella.app
Only 33 preset cities; any other venue needs manual coordinates and UTC offset

verdict: A competent, honest day-of timeline engine: every number I recomputed (sunsets for three cities within a minute of almanac values, the portrait block arithmetic, the greedy hair and makeup makespan, the 46-minute cocktail stretch) was right, and the durations sit inside normal wedding-photography and planning practice with a disclaimer. It does not meet the bar because verification scores 2 (two of three seeded mutations to core portrait durations survived all tests) and claims scores 2 (the 'about 30 minutes before sunset' promise is contradicted by its own worked example at 65 minutes, and llms.txt/sitemap point at wrong or relative URLs). Page was not loaded in a browser. Cheap fixes: add tests that pin the 35/26/30/15 minute blocks, state the real golden-hour offset in the guide, fix icsEscape, and use absolute URLs.
